The primary material of a candle is typically wax, which serves as the fuel source. Common types of wax include paraffin, beeswax, soy wax, and stearin. The wax is usually molded around a wick, which draws the liquid wax up via capillary action to be burned.

The genre of the document is descriptive narrative or literary prose. This is identified by the use of vivid sensory imagery ("hearty laughter," "faces flushed," "wind"), emotional tone ("pure, untainted joy," "poignant reminder"), and a focus on capturing a specific moment and atmosphere rather than conveying factual information or arguing a point. The language is figurative and evocative, characteristic of creative writing.
